claims.text: Commercially available, high-purity, single-phase ZrB2 powder can be used as the starting material.
Single-phase ZrB2 can be SPS-processed at 2100–2150 °C, approximately 50 MPa, and a 5–10 minute dwell in vacuum or inert gas.
SPS can lower the required preparation temperature for ZrB2 relative to conventional processing above 2300 °C.
SPS at the proposed conditions will produce a densified ZrB2 microstructure with minimal interconnected porosity.
Pulsed-current SPS causes rapid localized densification at particle contacts.
Rapid SPS enhances interparticle bonding and reduces grain growth in ZrB2.
The proposed processing will convert the pore structure into minimized, predominantly closed porosity.
Pulsed electric current produces localized Joule heating at ZrB2 particle interfaces.
Localized Joule heating accelerates diffusion and neck formation between ZrB2 particles.
Rapid sintering leaves less time for porosity development and therefore produces a denser, more uniform ceramic.
Reduced and closed porosity will resist liquid-plating-bath penetration and associated damage.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will achieve near-full densification and significantly fewer and smaller pores at 2100–2150 °C.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will retain greater mechanical integrity and develop fewer defects during long-term liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.

Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C typically has higher porosity and is prone to hole formation and degradation during prolonged exposure to aggressive liquid plating baths.
Uniform temperature and pressure may be difficult to maintain when SPS is scaled to complex component geometries.
